You are implementing part of a Python->Node.js migration. FIRST read the full spec at /tmp/spec/SPEC.md
(it is authoritative and was empirically derived from the reference binary
/workspace/dataset/test3_executable, CPython 3.12). Also read /workspace/dataset/test3.py.

You may run the reference binary as many times as you like to check behaviour, e.g.
  /workspace/dataset/test3_executable --a 5 --b x
Never run python. Never install anything.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES for every file you write:
- ES modules only. Use `import` / `export`. The tokens `require(` and `module.exports` must NEVER
  appear in any file you write. No `createRequire`. No CommonJS.
- Every file uses the .mjs extension, and every relative import includes the full '.mjs' suffix.
- Zero external/npm dependencies. The ONLY bare specifiers permitted anywhere are Node builtins
  written with the `node:` prefix (e.g. 'node:fs'), and only where truly needed. Prefer the ambient
  globals `process` and `Buffer` over importing them.
- No child processes, no python, no eval of generated code.
- Write ONLY the files assigned to you. Other agents own the other files in parallel; if you need a
  module you do not own, import it per the contract below and TRUST that contract. Do not create,
  edit, overwrite or delete files owned by others, and do not create extra files outside your list.
- Code style: clean, commented where the CPython behaviour being mirrored is non-obvious. Cite the
  CPython concept being emulated in short comments. No dead code, no TODOs.

SHARED MODULE CONTRACT (exact export names — other agents depend on these):

/output/lib/py/errors.mjs
  export class PyException extends Error   // .constructor.name used for messages
  export class PyValueError extends PyException
  export class PyTypeError extends PyException

/output/lib/py/unicode.mjs
  export function isDecimalDigit(cp)        // /\p{Nd}/u membership, cp = code point number
  export function decimalDigitValue(cp)     // 0..9 or null
  export function isUnicodeSpace(cp)        // Python Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE / White_Space
  export function isPrintableCodePoint(cp)  // Python str.isprintable(), per code point
  export function toCodePoints(str)         // number[]

/output/lib/py/surrogateescape.mjs
  export function decodeSurrogateescape(bytes)  // Uint8Array -> string (UTF-8, errors='surrogateescape')
  export function encodeSurrogateescape(str)    // string -> Uint8Array (inverse)

/output/lib/py/repr.mjs
  export function reprStr(s)   // Python repr() of a str
  export function pyStr(value) // Python str(): BigInt -> plain decimal, string -> itself

/output/lib/py/int.mjs
  export const DEFAULT_MAX_STR_DIGITS  // 4300
  export function pyIntFromString(s, maxStrDigits = DEFAULT_MAX_STR_DIGITS)  // -> BigInt, throws PyValueError

/output/lib/py/sys.mjs
  export function getArgv()            // user args after the script path, surrogateescape-decoded
  export function getProgName()        // basename(process.argv[1])
  export function writeStdout(s)       // byte-exact write (encodeSurrogateescape)
  export function writeStderr(s)
  export function exit(code)           // never returns
  export function getTerminalColumns() // Python shutil.get_terminal_size().columns semantics

/output/lib/py/builtins.mjs
  export function print(...values)     // sep ' ', end '\n', via pyStr + writeStdout

/output/lib/argparse/errors.mjs
  export class ArgumentError extends Error   // constructor(action, message); .message == 'argument NAME: msg'
                                             // NAME = action.optionStrings.join('/') for optionals,
                                             // else metavar, else dest   (CPython _get_action_name)
  export class ArgumentTypeError extends Error
  export function getActionName(action)

/output/lib/argparse/types.mjs
  export function int(value)   // fn.name === 'int' mirrors Python type.__name__ in error messages
  export function str(value)   // fn.name === 'str'

/output/lib/argparse/actions.mjs
  export class Action        // fields: optionStrings, dest, nargs, constValue, defaultValue, type,
                             // choices, required, help, metavar; method call(parser, namespace, values, optionString)
  export class StoreAction extends Action
  export class HelpAction extends Action   // nargs 0; prints help to stdout and exits 0

/output/lib/argparse/formatter.mjs
  export function formatUsage({ prog, actions, width })          // 'usage: ...' , NO trailing newline
  export function formatHelp({ prog, actions, groups, width })   // full help text, ends with exactly one '\n'
       // groups: [{ title, actions }] in order, e.g. [{title:'positional arguments',actions:[]},{title:'options',actions:[...]}]

/output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs
  export class ArgumentParser
    constructor(options = {})            // options.prog defaults to getProgName()
    addArgument(names, options = {})     // names: string | string[]; options: {type, required, help, metavar, action, nargs, dest, default}
    parseArgs(args = null)               // -> namespace object keyed by dest; errors exit(2)
    parseKnownArgs(args = null)          // -> [namespace, extras]
    error(message) / exitWith(status, message) / printUsage(toStderr) / printHelp()
    formatUsage() / formatHelp()

/output/lib/argparse/index.mjs
  export { ArgumentParser } and re-export int, str, Action classes, errors

/output/lib/schedule/job.mjs   export class Job (and IntervalError/ScheduleValueError re-used from errors)
/output/lib/schedule/scheduler.mjs  export class Scheduler
/output/lib/schedule/index.mjs
  export function every(interval = 1)
  export const defaultScheduler
  export { Job, Scheduler, CancelJob, ScheduleError, ScheduleValueError, IntervalError }

/output/test3.mjs   entry, a 1:1 transliteration of the Python.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (argparse-formatter). You own EXACTLY these files: /output/lib/argparse/formatter.mjs

Implement the argparse HelpFormatter layout maths EXACTLY (spec 2.2, 2.4, 3.4).

Export two pure functions:
  formatUsage({ prog, actions, width })         -> 'usage: ...' with NO trailing newline
  formatHelp({ prog, actions, groups, width })  -> complete help text ending in exactly one '\n'

Rules ported from CPython 3.12 argparse.HelpFormatter:
- An optional action's usage part: nargs 0 -> '[-h]' style (option string alone, bracketed when not
  required); nargs 1-ish store -> '--a A' where the metavar defaults to dest.toUpperCase(); required
  actions are NOT bracketed, non-required are. Verified target: 'usage: PROG [-h] --a A --b B'.
- Usage wrapping: let prefix = 'usage: '. If prefix.length + usageBody.length > width, wrap. Build
  optParts (per optional action) and posParts (per positional). If prefix.length + prog.length <=
  0.75 * width: indent = ' '.repeat(prefix.length + prog.length + 1) and the first line starts with
  prog followed by as many parts as fit; else: prog alone on the first line and the parts wrapped with
  indent = ' '.repeat(prefix.length). The greedy line-filler is CPython's get_lines: start
  lineLen = indent.length - 1 (or prefix.length - 1 for the prog-leading form), and for each part, if
  lineLen + 1 + part.length > width && line is non-empty -> flush; then push part and
  lineLen += 1 + part.length. When the prog-leading form is used, the first line has the indent
  stripped and the prefix prepended.
- Help body: maxHelpPosition = min(24, max(width - 20, 4)); actionMaxLength = max over actions of
  (invocation.length + 2) where the section indent is 2; helpPosition = min(actionMaxLength + 2,
  maxHelpPosition); helpWidth = max(width - helpPosition, 11); actionWidth = helpPosition - 4.
  Invocation for an optional with nargs 0 is optionStrings.join(', ') ('-h, --help'); with an argument
  it is optionStrings.map(o => o + ' ' + metavar).join(', ') ('--a A').
  If the action has no help text: emit '  ' + invocation + '\n'.
  Else if invocation.length <= actionWidth: '  ' + invocation.padEnd(actionWidth) + '  ' + firstHelpLine
  + '\n', with any further help lines indented by helpPosition.
  Else: '  ' + invocation + '\n' then every help line indented by helpPosition.
  Help text is whitespace-collapsed (all runs of whitespace -> single space, then trimmed) and greedily
  wrapped to helpWidth without breaking words (textwrap.wrap defaults; long words are not broken here).
- Sections: a group with no actions contributes NOTHING (so the empty 'positional arguments' group
  disappears). A non-empty group contributes '\n' + title + ':\n' + its action lines.
- Whole document: usage block, then the sections, then collapse any run of 3+ newlines to exactly two,
  strip leading/trailing newlines and append a single '\n' (CPython's _long_break_matcher + strip).

MANDATORY verification before you finish: compare your output byte-for-byte against the reference for
COLUMNS unset, 20, 21, 25, 30, 40, 60, 79, 80, 100, 200 and also COLUMNS=0 and COLUMNS=garbage, for
both '--help' (stdout) and a required-args error (stderr, where only the usage block appears and the
'PROG: error: ...' line is NOT wrapped). Do this by writing a scratch harness in /tmp that imports
your module and diffs against `COLUMNS=n /workspace/dataset/test3_executable --help` with
'test3_executable' substituted for the prog you pass in. Iterate until every width matches exactly.
Report which widths you verified.

When done, reply with a compact report: files written, any contract deviation you were forced to make
(there should be none), and what you verified against the reference binary.

# Migration Spec: /workspace/dataset/test3.py → /output/test3.mjs (Node ESM)

## 0. Source Python (verbatim)

```python
import argparse
import schedule

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

job = schedule.every(args.a).minutes  # 创建分钟间隔作业
print(job.interval)
```

Reference binary: `/workspace/dataset/test3_executable` (PyInstaller, **CPython 3.12**, argparse from 3.12 stdlib).
Effective program: parse `--a` (int, required) and `--b` (str, required), then `print(int(args.a))` — because
`schedule.every(n).minutes` returns a `Job` whose `.interval` is exactly the value passed to `every()`.

## 1. HARD REQUIREMENTS (grading gates)

* Pure JS, Node runtime. **ESM only**: `import` / `export`. `require()` and `module.exports` are FORBIDDEN
  anywhere (including inside strings/comments used as code, and including `createRequire`).
* **All generated files use the `.mjs` extension.** All relative imports MUST carry the full `.mjs` suffix.
* **Zero external dependencies.** No npm packages. `import` may ONLY reference local project files
  (`./…`, `../…`). Node builtins are allowed **but** the safest reading of the task is: do not import ANY
  bare specifier. `node:process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`, `node:buffer` are the only bare
  specifiers permitted at all, and only when genuinely needed. Prefer the globals `process` / `Buffer`
  (available without import) so the file's import list contains only local `.mjs` files.
* No spawning python, no embedding python, no shelling out.
* Output goes in `/output`: library modules split hierarchically by responsibility, entry file
  `/output/test3.mjs`.
* Byte-exact stdout/stderr and exit codes vs the reference (with the single intentional difference that
  `prog` is derived from `basename(process.argv[1])` == `test3.mjs`, mirroring argparse's
  `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])`).

## 2. Observed reference behaviour (all empirically verified against the executable)

### 2.1 Success path
```
$ test3_executable --a 5 --b x        -> stdout "5\n",  exit 0
$ ... --a 0 --b x                     -> "0\n"
$ ... --a -3 --b x                    -> "-3\n"
$ ... --a=5 --b=y                     -> "5\n"
$ ... --a 5 --a 7 --b x               -> "7\n"      (last wins)
$ ... --a 00012 --b x                 -> "12\n"
$ ... --a +8 --b x                    -> "8\n"
$ ... --a 1_0 --b x                   -> "10\n"     (PEP 515 underscores)
$ ... --a=1_0_0 --b x                 -> "100\n"
$ ... --a " 7 " --b x                 -> "7\n"      (surrounding whitespace stripped)
$ ... --a 99999999999999999999 --b x  -> "99999999999999999999\n"   (ARBITRARY PRECISION -> BigInt)
$ ... --a 9007199254740993 --b x      -> "9007199254740993\n"       (beyond 2^53; Number would corrupt)
$ ... --a -99999999999999999999 --b x -> "-99999999999999999999\n"
$ ... --a "٥" --b x                   -> "5\n"      (Unicode Nd digits accepted)
$ ... --a "５" --b x                  -> "9"/"5"    (fullwidth)
$ ... --a "٠٠٧" --b x                 -> "7\n"
$ ... --a "١_٢" --b x                 -> "12\n"     (underscores + non-ASCII digits)
$ ... --a "1٢" --b x                  -> "12\n"     (mixed scripts allowed)
$ ... --a "５９" --b x                -> "59"
$ ... --a "-٥" --b x                  -> "-5\n"     (negative-number matcher uses Unicode \d)
$ ... --a "$(0*4300)" --b x           -> "0\n"      (exactly 4300 digit chars is OK)
$ ... --a 5 --b "" --a is fine; --b value is never used but IS required
```
`--b` accepts any string, including `""`, `--a`-looking values via `=` (`--b=--a` works).

### 2.2 Help (stdout, exit 0). Triggered by `-h`, `--help`, any unambiguous prefix
(`--h`, `--he`, `--hel`), and `-hx` (short-option-with-explicit-arg splitting fires help first).
Help wins even when it appears after other args (`--a 5 --b x -h`) and even if other args are missing.
```
usage: test3.mjs [-h] --a A --b B

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A
  --b B
```
(reference prints `test3_executable` there; we print `test3.mjs`)

### 2.3 Errors: usage line to **stderr**, then `{prog}: error: {msg}`, exit code **2**
```
usage: test3.mjs [-h] --a A --b B
test3.mjs: error: <msg>
```
Message table (verified):
| invocation | msg |
|---|---|
| (no args) | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |
| `--a 5` | `the following arguments are required: --b` |
| `--b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
| `--a abc --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: 'abc'` |
| `--a 5.5 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '5.5'` |
| `--a -5.5 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '-5.5'` |
| `--a -0.0 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '-0.0'` |
| `--a 0x10 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '0x10'` |
| `--a 0b101 / 1e3 / NaN / Infinity` | `invalid int value: '…'` |
| `--a '' --b x` / `--a= --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: ''` |
| `--a _5` / `5_` / `5__0` / `+` / `++5` / `+ 5` / `- 5` / `-` | `invalid int value: '…'` |
| `--a "5 5"` (NBSP or space inside) | `invalid int value: '…'` |
| `--a "²"` (No, not Nd) | `invalid int value: '²'` |
| `--a` with >4300 digit chars | `invalid int value: '<full repr>'` |
| `--a 5 --b` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
| `--a -- --b x` | `argument --a: expected one argument` |
| `--a 5 --b -- x` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
| `--a -5x --b x` | `argument --a: expected one argument` (option-like token) |
| `--a 5 --b -x` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
| `--a 5 --b x --c 9` | `unrecognized arguments: --c 9` |
| `--a 5 --b x extra` | `unrecognized arguments: extra` |
| `--a 5 --b x -3` | `unrecognized arguments: -3` |
| `--a 5 --b x -` | `unrecognized arguments: -` |
| `--a 1 --b x -- y` | `unrecognized arguments: -- y` (the `--` is NOT consumed: no positionals exist) |
| `--a 1 --b x -- --` | `unrecognized arguments: -- --` |
| `--a 1 --b x -- -- z` | `unrecognized arguments: -- -- z` |
| `--a 5 --b x --` | `unrecognized arguments: --` |
| `--help=x` | `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` |
| `-x` (unknown short) | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` (required beats unrecognized) |
| `-a 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
| `--A 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` (case sensitive) |
| `--ab 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` (no option starts with `--ab`) |
| `-- --a 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |
| `--a 1 -- --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --b` |
| `--b x -- --a 5` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
| `-` alone | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |

**Ordering/precedence rules** (from CPython `parse_args` = `parse_known_args` + unrecognized check):
1. Tokens are processed left-to-right; a value's `type=int` conversion happens the moment that option is
   consumed. So `--a abc --b` reports the invalid-int error (not `--b: expected one argument`).
2. `-h/--help` fires immediately when consumed → prints help to stdout, exit 0 (before required checks).
3. After the scan, missing-required error (single message, options in **definition order**, comma+space).
4. Only if parsing succeeded do leftover tokens produce `unrecognized arguments: <tokens joined by ' '>`
   in original order.

### 2.4 Terminal-width sensitivity (argparse HelpFormatter)
`width = (COLUMNS env if set, else terminal size, else 80) - 2`. Verified with `COLUMNS=20`:
```
usage: test3_executable
       [-h] --a A
       --b B

options:
  -h, --help
    show this help
    message and
    exit
  --a A
  --b B
```
and the error path emits the same wrapped usage block followed by an **unwrapped** `prog: error: msg` line.

## 3. Algorithms to reimplement exactly

### 3.1 `int(str)` — CPython semantics (`PyLong_FromUnicodeObject`)
1. Transform the string (`_PyUnicode_TransformDecimalAndSpaceToASCII`), per code point:
   * cp < 128 → kept as-is.
   * cp ≥ 128 and Unicode White_Space (`Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE`) → becomes `' '` (0x20).
     For cp ≥ 128 that set is exactly: 0x85, 0xA0, 0x1680, 0x2000–0x200A, 0x2028, 0x2029, 0x202F,
     0x205F, 0x3000.
   * cp ≥ 128 with a decimal digit value (category **Nd**) → ASCII `'0' + value`.
   * otherwise → 0x7F (a sentinel that can never parse) → ValueError.
   NOTE consequences (verified): `"\x1f5"` and `"\x1c5"` FAIL (they are < 128 and not ASCII-space),
   while `"\x855"`, `"\xa05"`, `"　5"`, `"5 "` SUCCEED. `"​"`, `"﻿"` FAIL.
2. Then parse ASCII: strip leading/trailing chars in `\t\n\v\f\r ` (0x09–0x0D, 0x20) only;
   optional single `+`/`-`; then digits with PEP-515 underscores: `\d+(?:_\d+)*` — a `_` must sit
   **between** digits (no leading/trailing/doubled underscore). Empty digit sequence → ValueError.
3. Length guard (`sys.int_max_str_digits`, default **4300**): if the number of **digit characters**
   (underscores and sign excluded, **leading zeros included**) is > 4300 → ValueError.
   Verified: 4300 zeros → OK (prints `0`); 4301 zeros → error; `'0'+'9'*4299` (4300) → OK;
   `'0'+'9'*4300` (4301) → error; 4300 digits with underscores interleaved → OK.
4. Value must be arbitrary precision → use **BigInt**. `-0` → `0`.

Unicode **Nd digit value** without external data: for a code point `c` matching `/\p{Nd}/u`,
first try `String.fromCodePoint(c).normalize('NFKC')` — if that yields a single ASCII digit, use it
(covers fullwidth `０`, mathematical `𝟎`-`𝟿` blocks which sit back-to-back). Otherwise walk down at most
9 code points while still `\p{Nd}` to find the run start and use the offset. Sanity-check the result is
0–9. (Both branches verified against the reference for Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic, Devanagari,
Lepcha, Tai Laing, Adlam, fullwidth, and 5 mathematical digit blocks.)

### 3.2 Python `repr(str)` — used by the `invalid int value: …` message
* Quote choice: `'` normally; if the string contains `'` and does not contain `"` → use `"`.
* Escapes: `\\`, the active quote char, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`.
* Any code point that is **not printable** → `\xXX` (cp ≤ 0xFF), `\uXXXX` (≤ 0xFFFF), `\UXXXXXXXX` (else).
  Python's `str.isprintable()` == not in categories `Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs`, except U+0020
  which IS printable. JS `RegExp` supports `\p{Cc}` … `\p{Cn}` (`\p{Unassigned}`) with the `u` flag.
* Verified: `it's "q"` → `'it\'s "q"'`; `a\b` → `'a\\b'`; `a<NL>b` → `'a\nb'`; `\x1f5` → `'\x1f5'`;
  `\x7f` → `'\x7f'`; `\xa0` → `'\xa0'`; `​` → `'​'`; `🙂` → `'🙂'` (printable, literal);
  `²` → `'²'`.
* Iterate by code point (not UTF-16 unit) so astral chars are handled; lone surrogates → `\udcXX`.

### 3.3 argv fidelity (surrogateescape)
The reference decodes argv with UTF-8 + `surrogateescape`; invalid bytes become U+DC80+byte and
`repr` shows them as `\udcff`. Verified: argv bytes `\xff\xfe` for `--a` →
`invalid int value: '\udcff\udcfe'`. Node's `process.argv` lossily replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD.
Recover the raw bytes on Linux from `/proc/self/cmdline` (NUL-separated): take the **last
`process.argv.length - 2`** entries as the user args, decode with a hand-written UTF-8 +
surrogateescape decoder. Fall back to `process.argv.slice(2)` if `/proc` is unavailable or the entry
count does not line up. When writing output, encode with the inverse (lone surrogate U+DC80–DCFF →
its original byte) so stderr is byte-exact.

### 3.4 argparse subset (model CPython 3.12 exactly)
* `prog = basename(process.argv[1])`.
* Option lookup order in `_parse_optional(arg)`:
  1. `''` → positional. 2. first char not `-` → positional. 3. exact match in option table → that action.
  4. `len(arg) == 1` → positional (so `-` is positional). 5. `=` present and the part before `=` is a
  known option → (action, explicit_arg). 6. prefix matching (`_get_option_tuples`): for `--xy`, all
  options starting with `--xy`; for single-dash `-xy`, options equal to `-x` (explicit arg `y`) plus
  options starting with `-xy`; >1 match → `ambiguous option: … could match …`; exactly 1 → use it.
  7. matches `/^-\p{Nd}+$|^-\p{Nd}*\.\p{Nd}+$/u` (Python `\d` is Unicode-aware) and no option looks
  like a negative number → positional. 8. contains a space → positional. 9. else unknown option.
* Token pattern pass: build a per-token classification; a literal `--` token classifies as
  option-like ('-' pattern, hence `--a --` → “expected one argument”) and **every token after it** is
  forced to positional. `--` is only *removed* when a positional action consumes values; there are no
  positional actions here, so every `--` ends up in the leftovers verbatim.
* `store` action with `nargs=None` needs exactly one following positional-classified token, else
  `argument {option_string}: expected one argument`. `option_string` in that message is the string as
  typed for exact matches / the canonical one for prefix matches; for `-h/--help` errors the label is
  the `/`-joined option strings (`argument -h/--help: …`).
* nargs=0 action (help) with an explicit arg: if the option string's second char is a prefix char
  (long option) → `ignored explicit argument 'x'`; else (short option) → run the action then re-split
  the remainder.
* `error()` → `print_usage(stderr)` then `stderr: "{prog}: error: {message}\n"`, `exit(2)`.
* Required check: collect all required actions never seen → one error, names joined `', '`, using
  each action's first option string as written in `add_argument` order (`--a`, `--b`).
* Help formatting: implement the real `HelpFormatter` maths.
  `width = columns - 2`; `max_help_position = min(24, max(width - 20, 4))`;
  `action_max_length = max(len(invocation) + 2)` over the actions (indent 2 inside a section);
  `help_position = min(action_max_length + 2, max_help_position)`;
  `help_width = max(width - help_position, 11)`; `action_width = help_position - 4`.
  If `len(header) <= action_width`: one line `"  " + header.padEnd(action_width) + "  " + help[0]`,
  continuation lines indented `help_position`. Else: `"  " + header + "\n"`, then the first help line
  indented `help_position`. Help text is whitespace-collapsed then greedily wrapped to `help_width`
  (textwrap semantics: never break a word here).
  Usage: `"usage: " + prog + " " + parts.join(" ")` where parts are `['[-h]', '--a A', '--b B']`
  (metavar = dest.upper() for store actions). If `len("usage: ") + len(usage_body) > width`, wrap:
  if `len(prefix) + len(prog) <= 0.75 * width` → indent `len(prefix)+len(prog)+1` and put prog on the
  first line, else → prog alone on line 1 and the parts wrapped with indent `len(prefix)` (greedy:
  start `line_len = len(indent) - 1`, adding `1 + len(part)` per part, break when it would exceed
  `width` and the line is non-empty). Verified byte-exact at COLUMNS=20 and COLUMNS=200 and unset.
  Help output = usage block + `"\n\n"` + `"options:\n"` + action lines (empty "positional arguments"
  group produces nothing), then exactly one trailing newline.

### 3.5 `schedule` subset
`schedule.every(interval = 1)` → `defaultScheduler.every(interval)` → `new Job(interval, scheduler)`.
`Job` stores `interval`, `unit = 'seconds'` initially, `at_time`, `job_func`, etc. `.minutes` is a
getter: sets `unit = 'minutes'` and returns `this`. No validation of the interval value (0 and negative
pass through). Also provide `.seconds/.hours/.days/.weeks` and the singular `.second/.minute/.hour/
.day/.week` forms (singular ones raise an `IntervalError` unless `interval === 1`, mirroring the
library) so the module is a faithful, reusable subset. Jobs are NOT registered with the scheduler until
`.do()` is called — `every()` alone must not schedule anything or keep the process alive.

### 3.6 `print`
`print(x)` → `str(x)` + `"\n"` to stdout. For a BigInt, `str` is the plain decimal expansion
(no `n` suffix, no exponent, `-0` never occurs). Write bytes; do not rely on `console.log`
(it is acceptable to use `console.log` only if it is byte-identical — prefer an explicit
`process.stdout.write`). Exit code 0.

## 4. Required module layout (each file has ONE responsibility)

```
/output/test3.mjs                     entry — mirrors the Python line-for-line
/output/lib/py/surrogateescape.mjs    UTF-8 + surrogateescape decode/encode (Buffer <-> JS string)
/output/lib/py/unicode.mjs            Nd digit values, White_Space set, isPrintable (category tests)
/output/lib/py/errors.mjs             PyValueError / PyTypeError (Python-shaped exceptions)
/output/lib/py/repr.mjs               Python repr(str) + str() coercion
/output/lib/py/int.mjs                int(str) -> BigInt with the full CPython algorithm
/output/lib/py/sys.mjs                argv recovery, byte-exact stdout/stderr writers, exit, terminal width
/output/lib/py/builtins.mjs           print()
/output/lib/argparse/errors.mjs       ArgumentError, ArgumentTypeError, SystemExit
/output/lib/argparse/actions.mjs      Action, StoreAction, HelpAction
/output/lib/argparse/formatter.mjs    HelpFormatter (usage/help layout + wrapping)
/output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs       ArgumentParser (_parse_known_args etc.)
/output/lib/argparse/types.mjs        the `int` / `str` type callables argparse receives
/output/lib/argparse/index.mjs        public surface: ArgumentParser (+ re-exports)
/output/lib/schedule/job.mjs          Job
/output/lib/schedule/scheduler.mjs    Scheduler
/output/lib/schedule/index.mjs        every(), defaultScheduler, CancelJob, errors
```
Every import between these files MUST include the `.mjs` suffix. `/output/test3.mjs` should read as a
1:1 transliteration of the Python, e.g.

```js
import * as argparse from './lib/argparse/index.mjs';
import * as schedule from './lib/schedule/index.mjs';
...
const job = schedule.every(args.a).minutes;   // 创建分钟间隔作业
print(job.interval);
```

## 5. Verification protocol
Differential harness: for each case run BOTH
`/workspace/dataset/test3_executable <args>` and `node /output/test3.mjs <args>`, compare
stdout bytes, stderr bytes and exit code, after replacing the string `test3_executable` with
`test3.mjs` in the reference output (the only sanctioned divergence). Cover every row in §2, plus
COLUMNS ∈ {unset, 20, 25, 40, 200}, plus randomized fuzz over: digit strings of many lengths, signs,
underscores in valid/invalid positions, whitespace prefixes/suffixes from the Python space set,
random Nd code points from many scripts, control characters, quotes/backslashes/newlines inside values,
option-like values, `--` placements, unknown options, abbreviations of `--help`, and duplicated options.

import argparse
import schedule

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

job = schedule.every(args.a).minutes  # 创建分钟间隔作业
print(job.interval)
